guard: a proof killed mid-mutation leaves a record of what it broke, the next run names that run instead of blaming the operator's tree, and --restore-live puts the file back or refuses
why: THE DIRECTION AGAIN, and it is why a record rather than a handler. A handler covers the kills
that can be caught. SIGKILL cannot be, and it is the signal this repo's own reproof harness
sends to a proof that overruns its 140-minute deadline (mutation-reproof.mjs:44, :427-428,
:600-601). The file left behind is syntactically valid and deliberately sabotaged, every
surface reports a clean checkout, and the next measurement taken in that tree is meaningless
with nothing saying so.
Six mutations because the six properties fail differently and are repaired differently. A
record that is never written, a refusal that never fires, a record that is never cleared, a
restore that rounds the timestamp, a restore that trusts a backup it did not check, and a
stale record treated as live: each of those is a separate way for the mechanism to be present
and useless, and a suite that told them apart in its head but not in its output would be no
use to the person reading it.
MUTATION FOUR IS THE ONE WORTH ARGUING ABOUT and it is kept deliberately. Rounding the
timestamp is invisible to a byte comparison: the cell that grades it asserts the mtime and
nothing else can. `smoke:dist-freshness` is an mtime ORDERING test, so a restored file with a
fresh timestamp makes it name a package stale and refuse the chain at its first entry, for a
file nobody edited. That is the same defect the happy path's `utimesSync` already exists for.
THIS SUITE IS FAIL-FAST, so each mutation's named cell has to be the FIRST cell it reddens or
the verdict points at the wrong line. The ordering was checked one mutation at a time rather
than assumed: the record-cleared cell runs early, right after the first completed proof, because a record
left behind reddens `a dirty tree is refused` first otherwise; measured, not reasoned about.
NO top-level `completionMarker`, for the reason `restore-mtime.json` states about this same
suite: it is fail-fast, so its success banner is not printed on a red run, and a completion
marker pointed at it turns every genuine kill INCONCLUSIVE.
NOT ASSERTED, and recorded rather than implied: the cell `a proof that completes leaves no
record behind` cannot discriminate on a tree that has no records at all, so it
passes vacuously against the pre-fix tool. It is graded here by mutation three, which is the
only thing that gives it meaning.

mutations.name: the record is never written, so a killed run leaves no evidence
mutations.cell: ...and a record in tmpdir names the file, the mutation and the backup
mutations.expectRed: ...and a record in tmpdir names the file, the mutation and the backup

mutations.name: the startup refusal never fires, so the next run measures against the mutant
mutations.cell: the next run refuses by naming the previous run, not by calling the tree dirty
mutations.expectRed: the next run refuses by naming the previous run, not by calling the tree dirty

mutations.name: a verified restore leaves its record behind
mutations.cell: a proof that completes leaves no record behind
mutations.expectRed: a proof that completes leaves no record behind

mutations.name: --restore-live puts the bytes back and lets the timestamp move to now
mutations.cell: --restore-live puts the file back byte for byte, with its timestamp, and clears the record
mutations.expectRed: --restore-live puts the file back byte for byte, with its timestamp, and clears the record

mutations.name: --restore-live writes a backup it never checked over the file
mutations.cell: --restore-live refuses a backup that does not hash to the record, and leaves both in place
mutations.expectRed: --restore-live refuses a backup that does not hash to the record, and leaves both in place

mutations.name: a record whose file already matches it is treated as live, so git recovery becomes a trap
mutations.cell: a record whose file already matches it is cleared as stale and the run proceeds
mutations.expectRed: a record whose file already matches it is cleared as stale and the run proceeds
